tables.name: The Table of Ouch
tables.notes: The roll asks for actual damage suffered and whether Guts supplies a d10. Use only after a valid injury trigger. This table posts a reference result; use the actor injury workflow to record effects. Healing advances at mission starts and after full months of downtime; successful Surgery reduces healing time by 2.

results.text: Bleeding; Surgery DC 20; heals at scene end; gain 1d8 stress.
Broken limb; Surgery DC 20; healing 1d4 missions. GC chooses arm loss of use or Speed −20 ft.
Internal rupture; Surgery DC 25; healing 1d4 missions. Highest physical attribute −2 permanently; resolve ties randomly.
Maimed limb; Surgery DC 30; healing 1d6 missions. GC chooses arm loss of use or Speed −20 ft.
Brain damage; Surgery DC 35; healing 1d4 missions. Highest mental attribute −2 permanently; resolve ties randomly.
Massive system trauma; Surgery DC 40; healing 1d4 missions; permanently sickened.
Nerve damage; Surgery DC 45; healing 1d3 missions; permanently nauseated.
Spinal injury; Surgery DC 50; healing 1 mission; permanently paralyzed. Surgery is assumed after this mission.
Unlisted total: the printed table stops at 70. The GC resolves this result; do not cap it or invent another injury.
